Requirements:
- Classify every claim: "observation" (stated by a source), "inference", "hypothesis" or "forecast".
- Every claim needs at least one evidence link with relation "supports" and a verbatim quote. Add "contradicts" links for counter-evidence; do not omit evidence because it disagrees.
- Numbers in an "observation" must appear in the cited evidence text.
- Demand scenarios: forecast horizon 4 years (targetYear - baseYear between 3 and 5). State what is measured (unit demand vs revenue vs price) and its unit. Give bear/base/bull target values with assumptions, drivers, barriers and falsifying observations. Set "baselineValue" only when an evidence item states it: give "baselineEvidenceId" and "baselineQuote", a verbatim passage containing that number; otherwise null. Do NOT compute growth rates; they are derived from your values.
- Suppliers: only companies listed in JP or US with ticker AND exchange (JP: TSE, NSE, FSE, SSE; US: NYSE, NASDAQ, NYSE American, NYSE Arca, Cboe BZX, TXSE), and, for the supplier relationship itself, "evidence" entries each with a verbatim "quote" from a passage that names the company. Do not state figures about a supplier that the quoted evidence does not contain.
- Pricing power: report price realization separately from volume, mix, FX and input costs, in percent; give only figures that appear in the cited evidence and null for everything else. A margin improvement alone is not evidence of pricing power.
- 13F data are quarter-end reported holdings: say "newly reported holding" or "increase in reported position", never "bought".
- Do not state qualitative confidence as a probability.

Requirements:
- Classify every claim: "observation" (stated by a source), "inference", "hypothesis" or "forecast".
- Every claim needs at least one evidence link with relation "supports" and a verbatim quote. Add "contradicts" links for counter-evidence; do not omit evidence because it disagrees.
- Numbers in an "observation" must appear in the cited evidence text.
- Demand scenarios: forecast horizon 4 years (targetYear - baseYear between 3 and 5). State what is measured (unit demand vs revenue vs price) and its unit. Give bear/base/bull target values with assumptions, drivers, barriers and falsifying observations. Set "baselineValue" only when an evidence item states it: give "baselineEvidenceId" and "baselineQuote", a verbatim passage containing that number; otherwise null. Do NOT compute growth rates; they are derived from your values.
- Suppliers: only companies listed in JP or US with ticker AND exchange (JP: TSE, NSE, FSE, SSE; US: NYSE, NASDAQ, NYSE American, NYSE Arca, Cboe BZX, TXSE), and, for the supplier relationship itself, "evidence" entries each with a verbatim "quote" from a passage that names the company. Do not state figures about a supplier that the quoted evidence does not contain.
- Pricing power: report price realization separately from volume, mix, FX and input costs, in percent; give only figures that appear in the cited evidence and null for everything else. A margin improvement alone is not evidence of pricing power.
- 13F data are quarter-end reported holdings: say "newly reported holding" or "increase in reported position", never "bought".
- Do not state qualitative confidence as a probability.

Requirements:
- Classify every claim: "observation" (stated by a source), "inference", "hypothesis" or "forecast".
- Every claim needs at least one evidence link with relation "supports" and a verbatim quote. Add "contradicts" links for counter-evidence; do not omit evidence because it disagrees.
- Numbers in an "observation" must appear in the cited evidence text.
- Demand scenarios: forecast horizon 4 years (targetYear - baseYear between 3 and 5). State what is measured (unit demand vs revenue vs price) and its unit. Give bear/base/bull target values with assumptions, drivers, barriers and falsifying observations. Set "baselineValue" only when an evidence item states it: give "baselineEvidenceId" and "baselineQuote", a verbatim passage containing that number; otherwise null. Do NOT compute growth rates; they are derived from your values.
- Suppliers: only companies listed in JP or US with ticker AND exchange (JP: TSE, NSE, FSE, SSE; US: NYSE, NASDAQ, NYSE American, NYSE Arca, Cboe BZX, TXSE), and, for the supplier relationship itself, "evidence" entries each with a verbatim "quote" from a passage that names the company. Do not state figures about a supplier that the quoted evidence does not contain.
- Pricing power: report price realization separately from volume, mix, FX and input costs, in percent; give only figures that appear in the cited evidence and null for everything else. A margin improvement alone is not evidence of pricing power.
- 13F data are quarter-end reported holdings: say "newly reported holding" or "increase in reported position", never "bought".
- Do not state qualitative confidence as a probability.

Requirements:
- Classify every claim: "observation" (stated by a source), "inference", "hypothesis" or "forecast".
- Every claim needs at least one evidence link with relation "supports" and a verbatim quote. Add "contradicts" links for counter-evidence; do not omit evidence because it disagrees.
- Numbers in an "observation" must appear in the cited evidence text.
- Demand scenarios: forecast horizon 4 years (targetYear - baseYear between 3 and 5). State what is measured (unit demand vs revenue vs price) and its unit. Give bear/base/bull target values with assumptions, drivers, barriers and falsifying observations. Set "baselineValue" only when an evidence item states it: give "baselineEvidenceId" and "baselineQuote", a verbatim passage containing that number; otherwise null. Do NOT compute growth rates; they are derived from your values.
- Suppliers: only companies listed in JP or US with ticker AND exchange (JP: TSE, NSE, FSE, SSE; US: NYSE, NASDAQ, NYSE American, NYSE Arca, Cboe BZX, TXSE), and, for the supplier relationship itself, "evidence" entries each with a verbatim "quote" from a passage that names the company. Do not state figures about a supplier that the quoted evidence does not contain.
- Pricing power: report price realization separately from volume, mix, FX and input costs, in percent; give only figures that appear in the cited evidence and null for everything else. A margin improvement alone is not evidence of pricing power.
- 13F data are quarter-end reported holdings: say "newly reported holding" or "increase in reported position", never "bought".
- Do not state qualitative confidence as a probability.

Requirements:
- Classify every claim: "observation" (stated by a source), "inference", "hypothesis" or "forecast".
- Every claim needs at least one evidence link with relation "supports" and a verbatim quote. Add "contradicts" links for counter-evidence; do not omit evidence because it disagrees.
- Numbers in an "observation" must appear in the cited evidence text.
- Demand scenarios: forecast horizon 4 years (targetYear - baseYear between 3 and 5). State what is measured (unit demand vs revenue vs price) and its unit. Give bear/base/bull target values with assumptions, drivers, barriers and falsifying observations. Set "baselineValue" only when an evidence item states it: give "baselineEvidenceId" and "baselineQuote", a verbatim passage containing that number; otherwise null. Do NOT compute growth rates; they are derived from your values.
- Suppliers: only companies listed in JP or US with ticker AND exchange (JP: TSE, NSE, FSE, SSE; US: NYSE, NASDAQ, NYSE American, NYSE Arca, Cboe BZX, TXSE), and, for the supplier relationship itself, "evidence" entries each with a verbatim "quote" from a passage that names the company. Do not state figures about a supplier that the quoted evidence does not contain.
- Pricing power: report price realization separately from volume, mix, FX and input costs, in percent; give only figures that appear in the cited evidence and null for everything else. A margin improvement alone is not evidence of pricing power.
- 13F data are quarter-end reported holdings: say "newly reported holding" or "increase in reported position", never "bought".
- Do not state qualitative confidence as a probability.
